notes: Two-person photos stop blending faces, and the image stack gets a workbench. Group shots had two identity problems left: the written appearance anchor was singular and sender-only — 'the person shown' actively fought a two-person composition, and the second character's face rode on their LoRA alone — and both likeness LoRAs pushed at full strength on both faces, which is how two characters come out looking like siblings. Now every group member named in the scene gets their own anchor line ('Each person shown looks the same in every photo. Jess — … Harper — …'), on every engine including GLM, and whenever two or more identity LoRAs ride one photo each is damped to 0.75 — a sliver of likeness traded for much less blending, with the anchors pulling each face back toward its own person. And under Settings → Image generation there is now a Photo Lab: write the exact prompt (no director, no rewriting), tick exactly which LoRAs ride from everything configured anywhere — Settings and every character's cards, WHEN ignored on purpose — set each one's strength for the run without touching the cards, pick the engine (FLUX, your GPU, or GLM), aspect, and 18+ when mature mode is on, and paint. Optionally attach a character to append their appearance anchor and save keepers straight into their gallery. Built for exactly the question 'is it the LoRA, the strength, or the prompt?' — which used to take a staged conversation to answer.
